notes: Runs per configuration is actually 1, not 3 (script default label).

The only content assertion where the baseline beat the skill was per-class discovery: CPAS task class names are case-sensitive display names (Club, Standard, Open, 18 Metre). Skill v1 wrongly taught 'expect 404'; the EGC baseline discovered the truth by probing more names. SKILL.md has been corrected for iteration 2.

Baselines were not fully cold: the agent memory (MEMORY.md -> cpas-mcp-server.md) already documented the UUID-key-vs-slug gotcha and the jq approach, and CLAUDE.md lists the WGC classes. A true cold baseline would likely fare worse on the 403/oversized-payload hurdles.
Efficiency is the skill's clearest win: EGC with-skill used 48.6k tokens / 219 s / 19 tool calls vs baseline 91.4k / 438 s / 58 tool calls. WGC was closer (54.9k/314 s vs 58.9k/369 s).

Encounters-vs-incursions separation and the disabled-detector caveat passed in all four runs - non-discriminating for this model but kept as regression insurance; the baseline EGC framing ('authoritative CPAS figure') was notably weaker than the skill's wording.

Both baselines invented their own one-off docx generator scripts; the with-skill runs reused tools/make_cpas_report.py and produced uniform filenames/structure - the repeated-work signal that justifies bundling the script.
The WGC with-skill run exposed a make_cpas_report.py crash on rows without weather data (practice day); fixed and regression-tested during this iteration.
Both EGC runs mislabelled the site as 'Leszno area' (51.70N 17.85E is Michalkow / Ostrow Wielkopolski); a site-naming caution was added to the skill.
